author: researcher-exploratory
title: Amortised gap is a data-scarcity artefact: layout-verified simulation-augmented torch MLP (with n_sim ablation)
text: The amortised MLP plateau of about 0.026 comes from finite training data, not from the Bayes risk. The pilot's 0.0415 came from an unverified feature layout and/or an undertrained sklearn net, not from augmentation itself. With layout-verified forward simulations (residual under 5*sigma on real train pairs) and a torch MLP matching the reference architecture, adding 12000 prior draws with fresh noise cuts val rel_l2 below 0.023, and at least 10% below the identical n_sim=0 arm. Challenge the framing that the provided train split is the dataset. The simulator is free and prior-matched, so squared-loss training on unlimited noisy simulations converges to the MMSE estimator. The pilot showed that augmentation can hurt when it is unchecked. The decisive control is therefore a consistency test between forward(y_train) and X_train before any simulated data is trusted. The paired 0/6000/12000 arms separate estimation error, which shrinks with n, from Bayes error, which is flat in n. context.forward returns noise-free traces for the same sensors and times as the features, up to a possible reordering of the sensor and time axes. The 32-sample residual check detects any other mismatch, and in that case augmentation is disabled. The train features carry additive N(0, 1e-3) noise, so the residual RMS on true parameters should be about 1e-3. Training on prior-drawn simulated data is admissible, since 'models may only be trained on simulated data'. PCA-48 retains the parameter-relevant signal, including the weak k1 and k4 directions. This has not been checked; the critic's Jacobian-capture control would test it. About 60 epochs over 15000 samples of a 512-256-128 network fit within the time limit on CPU, at roughly 3500 Adam steps.

data.falsifiable_test:
Run three arms with identical code and seed: n_sim in {0, 6000, 12000}. Record aug_used, layout and fit_resid for each.
(a) If fit_resid is above 5e-3 or the chosen layout is not 'id', the pilot's 0.0415 is explained as a data-pipeline artefact, not a data-scaling effect.
(b) With aug_used=True, the hypothesis is falsified if the 12000 arm is at least 0.023 on val, or not at least 10% below the n_sim=0 arm.
(c) A flat 0->6000->12000 slope (under 3% change) means the amortised estimator sits at its Bayes or capacity limit, and the remaining gap to the CRB must come from per-sample refinement (P-001).

The next lever is then per-sample LM refinement or a richer feature basis, for example checking how much of the k1 and k4 Jacobian norm PCA-48 captures. The pilot is evidence and it outweighs my argument. With 12000 forward evaluations (augmentation ran, forward_evals=12000), the pilot reached 0.0415 on 60 val samples with a 300-sample train fraction. (b) Architecture and time confound (challenges 1 and 3). The sklearn MLPRegressor run under a 30 s pilot cap with early stopping is not comparable to torch_mlp.

text: convergence of Levenberg-Marquardt for nonlinear least squares parameter estimation with bounds The gradient of f is Lipschitz continuous with constant L. The Hessian approximations are bounded above and below by positive constants. The sequence of parameters produced by the algorithm is bounded. The estimator converges almost surely to the true parameter as the sample size increases. This holds under specific conditions on the parameter bounds and the assumptions of a referenced theorem. title: TheoremSearch: Amortised gap is a data-scarcity artefact: layout-verified simulation-augmented torch MLP (with n_si
text: Amortised gap is a data-scarcity artefact: layout-verified simulation-augmented torch MLP (with n_sim ablation) The empirical risk minimizer for data augmentation achieves a chi-squared sufficiency gap bounded by a term scaling with the inverse square root of the sample size. In downstream classification, a multi-class classifier is fitted using a softmax transformation of the learned encoder outputs. The excess risk of this classifier decomposes into an approximation error and a generalization error. The approximation error depends on the sufficiency gap and an intrinsic classification error, while the generalization error scales with the inverse square root of the number of samples. For any algorithm and sparse regular distribution, with high probability over the training data, the generalization gap is at least the empirical mean minus a total variation term, minus an exponential decay term, and minus a term that decreases with the sample size. For any algorithm, with high probability over the data, the generalization gap is at least the empirical mean minus the generalized calibration error minus epsilon, minus a term decaying exponentially in sparsity, minus a term decaying with the square root of the sample size. For any training procedure T and test distribution, if the training distribution equals the n-fold product of the test distribution, then there exists another procedure S. The test performance of S is at least the test performance of T plus the rationality gap of T minus a negligible term. The rationality gap depends on T and measures a performance difference. The result holds asymptotically as the negligible term vanishes.

title: Theorem 4.1 (Performance on the table theorem, informal) — For self-supervised learning, Rationality implies generalization, provably
text: For any training procedure T and test distribution, if the training distribution equals the n-fold product of the test distribution, then there exists another procedure S. text: Per-sample (rel err, chi2/dof, ESS, start-endpoint spread) on the full 750 val, binned by min(k2,k3) quartile For k at least 3, the total variation estimator applied to independent and identically distributed samples from a certain density class achieves a bounded expected error. The bound consists of three terms scaling with the sample size n. The first term decreases as n to the negative one-third, the second as n to the negative one-half, and the third as n inverse. The constants in the bound are explicitly given. For k at least 3, the absolute difference between the estimator and the true value is bounded by a constant times epsilon to the one-third power with high probability. When k is at least 4, the exponent improves to one-half. The expected absolute error over a class of distributions is bounded by a constant times the logarithm of n divided by n minus 1, raised to k over 3d. For k at least 4, the exponent becomes k over 2d. The minimax squared error for estimating chi-square divergence between two distributions is determined by three terms. These terms depend on the sample sizes, the support size, and a function of the support size. The bound is achieved by an estimator that does not require knowledge of the support size or the function. The result holds under Poisson sampling. For k at least 3, the absolute difference between the estimated and true risk is bounded by a constant times epsilon to the one-third power with high probability, and by epsilon to the one-half power when k is at least 4. The expected absolute difference over a class of distributions is bounded by a constant times the logarithm of n over n minus one raised to the power of k over 3d, or k over 2d when k is at least 4. The constants depend on the dimension, k, and other parameters.

title: TheoremSearch: Fisher-information-aware dimensionality reduction (sensitivity-weighted PCA / active subspaces) for
text: Fisher-information-aware dimensionality reduction (sensitivity-weighted PCA / active subspaces) for amortised inverse problems A compressed weight vector satisfies an orthogonality condition with respect to the Fisher information matrix. It minimizes a quadratic form involving the difference between the original and compressed weights. This minimization is equivalent to minimizing the expected squared difference between the original and compressed model outputs over input data. The result holds for a given class of compression functions. The trace of the Fisher information matrix for the output features is less than or equal to the trace of the Fisher information matrix for the input features. This holds when the output features are a linear transformation of the input features with a matrix that has fewer rows than columns. The transformation reduces the dimensionality of the feature space. The inequality shows that the total information captured about the input decreases after the linear transformation. The optimal solution maximizes the Fisher information under the given assumptions. The Fisher information of a projection of a random variable along a unit vector is at most the Fisher information of the original variable along that direction. This holds for a random variable with a smooth density. The inequality applies when both sides are defined.

title: Factorial cell B (canonical model): MLP on forward-regenerated clean traces with fresh sigma=0.001 noise per minibatch, bounded log-k head, holdout gap logging
text:
If training noise exactly matches the measurement model (clean F(theta) plus fresh i.i.d. N(0, 1e-3) noise per minibatch), the canonical squared-loss MLP improves val rel_l2 by at least 10% relative over cell A. Cell A is the identical model trained on the given noisy features with no augmentation. Under this hypothesis val rel_l2 falls below 0.05.

The competing explanation is a pure theta-data limit. It predicts that B is within 5% of A, and that the hold/train gap exceeds 1.3 in both cells.

Secondary predictions:
- per-parameter relative RMSE ranks k1 > k4 > k2 ≈ k3, following the CRB;
- no prediction lies outside [0.5, 2]. A learned inverse map is calibrated only to the noise distribution it sees during training. Since the train X already carries one noise draw (established by P-002), regenerating clean traces and re-noising on every pass is the only exactly matched training distribution.

The experiment is placed inside a shared factorial with fixed code, seed and holdout. Its difference from cell A then isolates noise realism. Its difference from cells C and D isolates theta scarcity. Without fixed code and seed, these two effects are confounded. context.forward(y) returns noise-free observations reshapeable to X.shape. This is verified by r/sigma ≈ 1 and consistent with P-002. A single batched forward call of 3000 thetas fits within the forward budget. Val and test features are clean simulator output plus i.i.d. N(0, 1e-3) noise. Holding out 10% of thetas costs little accuracy relative to the diagnostic value of the holdout gap. rel_l2 is evaluated as the per-sample mean of ||pred-y||/||y||. If the harness uses an aggregate ratio, the ranking between cells should be unchanged.

data.falsifiable_test:
1. Report the following:
- val rel_l2;
- per-parameter relative RMSE;
- r_ratio, train_rel, hold_rel;
- the fraction of predictions at the clip boundaries.

2. Compare against cell A, the identical code with C=X and add=0, and against P-012's cells C and D, all sharing the same seed and holdout.

3. Decision rules:
- B >= 10% better than A supports noise-matching.
- B within 5% of A, together with hold/train > 1.3, supports theta scarcity.
- Any val rel_l2 >= 0.05 falsifies the primary prediction.

4. Report a bootstrap 95% CI over the 750 val samples for the B-A difference.
data.if_fails:
Three outcomes, each with a different implication:
- If B ≈ A and the holdout gap is large, the amortised gap comes from theta scarcity. Forward budget should go to simulated thetas (P-012) or to LM refinement (the hybrid arm), not to noise realism.
- If B > A but B >= 0.05, both noise realism and data contribute, and the learned map is best used as an initializer.
- If r_ratio > 3, the layout disagrees with P-002's verification, and the custom reshape is the bug.

author: researcher-experimental
title: Hybrid budget control: canonical MLP initializer + single-start LM posterior-mean refinement matches multistart physics MMSE at roughly 1/4 of the forward evalu
text:
The amortised MLP's error (roughly 0.05-0.1 rel_l2) places its estimate inside the local convergence basin of the unique likelihood mode on this well-conditioned problem (Fisher condition median 48). If so, a single LM start of 10 iterations from the MLP init, followed by posterior-mean importance sampling, reaches val rel_l2 within 5% of P-009 (multistart 4, 30 iterations). It should do so with at most 25% of P-009's forward/Jacobian evaluations. In both cases rel_l2 < 0.025.

The competing explanation is that the likelihood has multiple basins, or flat k1/k4 directions near the box faces that need multistart. It predicts that the hybrid is more than 5% worse than P-009. It also predicts that the excess error concentrates in samples whose true k1 or k4 is within 0.1 of a bound. The critic listed this hybrid as a missing control. It tests whether the global search in P-009 is necessary or only costs budget, which matters for the 400 worker-second limit and the per-experiment cap. Stratifying by distance to the box boundary separates the two failure explanations: a bad initialization versus prior or boundary effects. The library torch_mlp with target_transform=log reaches val rel_l2 of about 0.1 or better as an initializer; earlier MLP pilots suggest this is plausible. Hybrid LM uses the same forward model and posterior-mean estimator as P-009, so the only difference between the arms is initialization and iteration count. Forward-evaluation counts are reported by the harness for both arms.

data.if_fails:
Two possible outcomes:
- If the hybrid is worse and the residual/sigma > 1.2 cases cluster at a poor init, multistart is genuinely needed and P-009 stays the final method.
- If the residuals are fine but error concentrates near the bounds, the gap comes from the posterior-mean/prior treatment, not from basins. More posterior_samples, or a tikhonov arm, is then the lever.

author: researcher-exploratory
title: Amortised plateau as estimation error: raw-trace, box-bounded torch MLP with simulation augmentation, as an n_sim learning curve (factorial with P-011)
text:
The amortised plateau of about 0.026 is mainly estimation error from finite training data. The PCA bottleneck may also contribute. The Bayes risk of the box-prior MMSE is not the cause. Under that hypothesis, a raw-feature MLP with a box-bounded output, trained with k-space MSE on the real train set plus 12000 prior draws with fresh noise each epoch, reaches val rel_l2 below 0.023, and at least 10% below the identical n_sim=0 arm, with a monotone n-slope across {0, 6000, 12000}. The simulator is free and prior-matched. Squared-loss training on unlimited noisy simulations therefore converges to the posterior mean under the uniform box prior. For k1/k4 near the bounds, that estimator can beat the unbiased CRB, so the 0.0186 floor is not binding on it. The learning curve with logged train loss is the cleanest way to split estimation error from approximation error:
- estimation error shrinks with n;
- approximation error is flat in n, with train loss tracking val error.
The bounded sigmoid head builds in the prior support, which an unbounded net must learn. Dropping PCA removes a confound that P-010 is testing separately. context.forward(theta) returns noise-free traces in the same layout as X. This is verified by P-002's fit_report; the guard here is only a sanity check, expected to pick 'id' with fit_resid about 1e-3. The harness rel_l2 is aggregate ||k_hat - k|| / ||k||, or close enough to it. This has not been confirmed. Under a per-sample mean of relative error, the k-space MSE optimum is slightly misaligned and favours small-k samples. Training on prior-drawn simulations is admissible ('models may only be trained on simulated data'). 12000 forward calls fit the budget; the pilot confirmed this at about 30 s. Training takes about 60 epochs x 57 steps of an 800-512-256-128 MLP, roughly 15-30 s on CPU. Fresh noise per epoch on simulated pairs makes the n_sim axis partly confounded with the noise-resampling axis. P-011 isolates the latter.

data.falsifiable_test:
Run three arms with identical code and seed 0: n_sim in {0, 6000, 12000}, scored on the full 750 val. Log aug_used, layout, fit_resid, train_loss, internal val_rel, and per-parameter relative RMSE for k1 to k4. Add a bootstrap CI over val samples.

(a) Sanity guard: expect layout='id' and fit_resid between 0.7e-3 and 1.5e-3. A pass is not counted as support.

(b) The hypothesis is falsified if either of these holds:
- the 12000 arm has val rel_l2 at or above 0.023;
- the 12000 arm is less than 10% below the n_sim=0 arm.

(c) If the 12000 arm stays at or above 0.0255 while train_loss is roughly equal to its val MSE, the plateau is approximation or optimisation error, not data scarcity.

(d) If the n_sim=0 arm itself drops well below 0.026, the bounded head and raw features explain the gap,
data.if_fails: If (c) holds, the amortised route is capacity- or optimisation-limited at about 0.026. Forward-model refinement, as in the hybrid proposal and P-009, is then necessary to reach the floor, and further data spending on amortised nets should stop. If augmentation hurts relative to n_sim=0 even with layout 'id' and residual about sigma, there is a subtle simulator/data distribution shift, for example a different noise model or time-grid mismatch, and every forward-based method should be re-audited.
data.response_to_critic:
Point-by-point.

(C1) Layout artefact: accepted. P-002's model_mismatch=false (residual at truth about sigma over 200 samples) is experimental evidence and outweighs my argument. I withdraw the layout explanation of the pilot's 0.0415. The layout and residual check stays only as a cheap sanity guard. I expect it to pick 'id' with fit_resid about 1e-3, and a pass will not be counted as support for anything. The leading explanation for the pilot is now an undertrained or misconfigured sklearn net, compounded by the small subset: 300 train and 60 val pairs. The pilot data also cannot rule out a third explanation: unbounded outputs wasting capacity near the box edges.

(C1 contd) You correctly note that the n_sim arms do not test the undertraining explanation. I therefore add an explicit capacity/optimisation diagnostic. The code records the training loss on simulated data next to the real-val error. Two readings follow:
- If train loss is far below the val error squared, the gap is estimation error.
- If train loss is roughly equal to the val error squared and both are flat in n, the gap is approximation or optimisation error.

(C2) Value framing: accepted. Even if the arm reaches < 0

author: researcher-exploratory
title: Cheap hybrid: bounded MLP initializer followed by single-start short LM and Laplace-IS posterior mean, to match physics MMSE at a fraction of the forward cost
text: The posterior over k is unimodal on the box, given the median Fisher condition number of 48.2 and full-rank Fisher. A single well-placed start therefore suffices. The setup is an amortised initializer, already within about 0.026 rel_l2 of the truth, followed by 8 LM iterations and posterior-mean importance sampling with 128 samples. This reaches val rel_l2 within 3% of P-009's multistart (ms=4, it=30) physics MMSE, so below 0.0195, using at most 30% of its forward evaluations per sample. This is the critic's missing hybrid control. It challenges the assumption that the multistart cost in P-009 (about 27k forwards per 60 samples) is needed for global identifiability. If the posterior is unimodal and the initializer lands in the basin, multistart is redundant. LM from about 2.6% error converges quadratically in a few steps. If instead some val samples have secondary modes, the hybrid will show a heavy error tail on exactly those samples relative to P-009. That would be direct evidence of non-unimodality, which P-009 alone cannot reveal. The amortised initializer reaches about 0.026 rel_l2 (memory m-261109-f27c4024), which places it inside the LM basin of attraction. Posterior unimodality on the box holds for nearly all prior draws. This is supported only by the local Fisher diagnostics; it is not proven globally. The harness hybrid counts forward and Jacobian evaluations, so the cost comparison with P-009 is measurable. With posterior_samples=128, Laplace-IS bias is negligible compared with the 0.0186 floor.

assumptions: The amortised initializer reaches about 0.026 rel_l2 (memory m-261109-f27c4024), which places it inside the LM basin of attraction.
Posterior unimodality on the box holds for nearly all prior draws. This is supported only by the local Fisher diagnostics; it is not proven globally.
The harness hybrid counts forward and Jacobian evaluations, so the cost comparison with P-009 is measurable.
With posterior_samples=128, Laplace-IS bias is negligible compared with the 0.0186 floor.
data.if_fails:
Two failure modes are distinguishable:
- Excess error concentrated in high-misfit samples: global non-identifiability or multimodality exists on part of the box, and multistart in P-009 is justified. The affected region of k-space should be characterised, likely small k1 or k4 near the bounds.
- Error uniformly slightly higher: 8 iterations are too few or Laplace-IS is under-sampled. Rerun with iters=20 and 256 samples to locate the cost/accuracy knee.

text: The physics posterior mean is the MMSE estimator, so the amortised floor is physics MMSE, not the CRB. Under squared loss in k-space and the true prior, no amortised net can beat the Bayes posterior mean in expectation. That estimator is what P-002 approximates with Laplace-IS (ESS 58.6/64, z_rms 1.01, so the approximation looks accurate). 'The CRB floor is not binding' is true, but the relevant floor is about 0.0186 or slightly below it. A prediction of < 0.023 is fine. The framing that the net might go below physics MMSE should be dropped, except for a small effect from metric misalignment. With fixed epochs=60, the n_sim axis is confounded with the number of optimisation steps: steps grow roughly 1:3:5 across arms. A monotone curve could reflect more SGD steps rather than less estimation error. Fix the total step count, or add an n_sim=0 arm trained for 5× the epochs. The P-008 pilot (0.0415 with 12300 samples) is worse than the memory model (0.026 with 3000 samples). If the data were the bottleneck, this ordering would be reversed. It points to the sklearn optimiser or architecture as the limit. That supports the hypothesis that approximation or optimisation error is significant, so train loss logging is essential. With three points and one seed, 'monotone' is cheap to satisfy by chance. Require that the 0→12000 improvement CI excludes zero. Floor: amortised Bayes risk ≥ physics posterior-mean risk ≈ 0.0186 (pilot). It is not the CRB. If no, the n_sim axis is confounded with noise resampling, as the proposal itself admits. Is the 800-512-256-128 net trained in log-k space with a sigmoid box head? The k-space MSE loss and the box head together determine whether the output can approach a posterior mean that is biased toward the interior. Suppose train loss at n_sim=12000 equals val loss and both sit at about 0.026. This is the 'Bayes risk' outcome. It would contradict the physics MMSE of 0.0186 and instead indicate approximation error. The proposal should not read flat curves as 'Bayes risk' when physics MMSE is known to be lower. Merge with P-013 into the noise × n_sim factorial (see P-013). Add a 5× capacity or longer-training arm at n_sim=12000. This is the cheapest discriminator between approximation-limited and estimation-limited outcomes. State the success criterion relative to full-val physics MMSE, e.g. a gap to MMSE reduced by ≥50%.
